items.title: Fee-Based Onramp Routing Is Costing You Business
items.tldr: Routing purely on the lowest fee ignores the thing that actually matters, which is whether the payment succeeds at all.

items.title: Stablecoin Yield Explained: Why Rates Beat Traditional Banks
items.tldr: The gap is not magic, it is a shorter chain of intermediaries each taking a cut. Traces where the extra return comes from and where it is borrowed.

items.title: How to Evaluate Stablecoin Yield Risks: A Guide for Fintechs
items.tldr: Five risks to work through before shipping a yield product, starting with counterparty exposure and liquidity.

items.title: How Stablecoins Are Reshaping B2B Payments
items.tldr: Business-to-business transfer is the fastest-growing use for stablecoins and least discussed. Why the pain there is sharper than consumer payments.

items.title: Lessons in Entrepreneurship With Ben Huh
items.tldr: A founder conversation that stays concrete about early decisions rather than drifting into advice. Useful if you are near the start of building something.

items.title: A Fund GP on the Crypto Founder's Zero-to-One Journey
items.tldr: The investor's side of very early crypto companies: what gets funded, what does not, and which signals a GP is actually reading.

items.title: Reputation in Web2 vs Web3, Explained
items.tldr: Your Uber rating is worthless on Airbnb and LinkedIn endorsements mean nothing on Discord. A long piece on why reputation stays fenced in.

items.title: Why Reputation Is the New Currency in Web3
items.tldr: Pseudonymous systems remove the usual anchors for trust, then must rebuild something. Works through what a portable reputation would need to satisfy.

items.title: Private Proof-of-Funds for OTC Deals and Launchpad Access
items.tldr: Using zkTLS to prove you meet an exchange's balance threshold without revealing the account or the balance.

items.title: A Complete Guide to Orca's Liquidity Terminal
items.tldr: A full walkthrough of tooling built to turn liquidity provision from guesswork into measured allocation. Useful even if you provide it elsewhere.

items.title: The Full Picture for Liquidity Provision in One Place
items.tldr: Covers pool filters, position monitoring and the numbers an LP actually needs to see. Good on why scattered information leads to bad range decisions.

items.title: Orca Is Becoming a Platform for Every Capital Allocator on Solana
items.tldr: A DEX arguing its own ceiling is higher than exchange. Worth reading as a statement of where AMM infrastructure thinks it is heading next.

items.title: How to Create a Perp DEX Without Writing Any Code
items.tldr: Spinning up an exchange in minutes on shared liquidity. Worth reading for which parts of an exchange are commodity infrastructure now.

items.title: Multi-Collateral Margin
items.tldr: Funding a position with USDC, USDT or ETH sounds like a convenience feature and is really a risk-engine change. Covers what has to be handled behind it.

items.title: Permissionless Listings on Orderly
items.tldr: Letting any venue list and manage its own assets moves the listing decision away from a central gatekeeper, and moves the risk with it.

items.title: Trading Real World Assets Without a Broker
items.tldr: What changes when exposure to commodities or equities is taken directly onchain rather than through an intermediary - including what the broker did.

items.title: Pass-Through Taxation for Foreign-Owned US LLCs, in Plain English
items.tldr: Separates what a non-US owner genuinely owes from what they merely have to file, which are very different lists and the source of most of the confusion.

items.title: Best State to Form a US LLC as a Foreigner
items.tldr: Wyoming against Delaware, and the cases where neither is right. Structured as a decision guide rather than a ranking, which is what the question needs.

items.title: LLC for a Token Launch: The Legal Setup Founders Miss
items.tldr: Who owns the treasury, who owns the IP, and what the entity is for. These get decided by accident before a launch far more often than deliberately.

items.title: Wallet Entropy and the Coldcard Incident, Explained
items.tldr: A silent fallback in the random number generator cut seed entropy from 128 bits to 40, which is the difference between unbreakable and brute-forceable.

items.title: How Large Trades Impact Your Execution (And How to Avoid It)
items.tldr: Size moves the price against you before the trade even completes. Explains how splitting an order over time reduces slippage and where that stops helping.

items.title: Guarded Swaps: Best Price Without the Fail Rate
items.tldr: RFQ and proprietary AMM quotes are often the best price available and the first to expire between click and confirmation.

items.title: The End of the Bridge: A Cross-Chain Execution Layer
items.tldr: Argues the bridge should disappear behind execution rather than being a step the user performs. Covers hybrid execution, MEV protection and gasless flows.

items.title: What Is a DATCO? A Digital Asset Treasury Guide
items.tldr: How digital asset treasury companies raise capital, deploy it, and the mNAV arithmetic deciding whether they trade at a premium or a discount.

items.title: Hyperliquid Fees Explained: Developer Costs
items.tldr: Long and specific on what it costs to build on Hyperliquid: infrastructure, HyperEVM gas, HIP-3 and HIP-4, and the ways those costs can be offset.

items.title: Earn API: Automated USDC Yield in Your App
items.tldr: Creating and closing yield strategies over plain HTTP, non-custodially, across seven chains. Interesting for how thin the integration surface has become.

items.title: Wells Fargo's Tokenized Deposits Show Where Settlement Is Heading
items.tldr: A major bank offering round-the-clock dollar-to-pound transfers for corporate clients. Tokenised deposits differ from stablecoins in ways this makes clear.

items.title: Cloudflare Starts Wallet Rollout for AI Agents
items.tldr: Programmable wallets from an infrastructure company already sitting in front of much of the web. Notable for who is doing it, not what is built.

items.title: How BlackRock's Tokenized Treasury Funds Are Changing Stablecoin Reserves
items.tldr: Two money market funds aimed specifically at backing stablecoins. A sign reserve management is becoming its own product category.

items.title: AI Agents Using Credit Cards: Is It Safe? Will It Work?
items.tldr: Card rails assume a human is present and can dispute a charge later. What breaks when the cardholder is software, and which protections stop applying.

items.title: Agentic Commerce: How AI Agents Pay
items.tldr: Surveys the payment methods an autonomous agent can actually use today, and what each one requires the merchant on the other side to accept.

items.title: Business Credit Cards for SMEs: A Spend Control Guide
items.tldr: Long and practical on what matters after issuing cards: limits, approval routing and catching unauthorised spend before the statement arrives.

items.title: How to Organize a Web3 Hackathon That Creates Real Builder Outcomes
items.tldr: Very long and genuinely operational: goals, tracks, promotion, judging, and the follow-through that decides whether anything survives the weekend.

items.title: How to Design Web3 Hackathon Tracks and Prizes
items.tldr: Track design quietly determines who bothers entering and whether judging can be fair. Works through both, which most hackathon advice skips entirely.

items.title: Web3 Hackathon Timeline: A Step-by-Step Planning Guide
items.tldr: The whole run in order, from strategy and promotion through onboarding, submissions and reporting. Useful even if you are only attending.

items.title: CeFi vs DeFi Loans: Which Is Better?
items.tldr: The most useful entry here: what changes about custody, liquidation and recourse depending on who is actually holding your collateral.

items.title: Account Abstraction and the Future of DeFi
items.tldr: Approaches account abstraction from the borrowing side rather than the wallet side, which surfaces different questions about who can act and when.

items.title: How to Take Out a Crypto-Backed Loan, Step by Step
items.tldr: Borrowing against crypto rather than selling it changes your tax position and adds a liquidation price you now have to watch.

items.title: Fearless Concurrency With Rust
items.tldr: The post that explained why Rust's ownership rules eliminate data races at compile time rather than at runtime.

items.title: Stability as a Deliverable
items.tldr: Treats not breaking your users as a feature to be engineered rather than a promise to be made. The reasoning here shaped how Rust ships to this day.

items.title: The Road to Rust 1.0
items.tldr: What the team decided had to be true before calling a language finished enough to commit to. Useful reading for anyone versioning a protocol or an API.

items.title: 594.5 BTC Gone: When Trusted Hardware Fails
items.tldr: Around 500 addresses drained in a short window, 1,324 UTXOs in total. A careful write-up of trusted hardware turning out to be the weakness.

items.title: The Triple-A Attack and a Review of July's Security Incidents
items.tldr: A month of failures collected in one place, starting with a treasury breach. Incidents in aggregate reveal patterns individual post-mortems miss.

items.title: Why a Recovery Phrase Must Be Truly Random
items.tldr: A seed is only as strong as the entropy behind it, and hardware random number generation is where that quietly goes wrong.

items.title: Security Tips and Best Practices for Web3 Wallets
items.tldr: Broad but practical: approvals, phishing, backup handling and the everyday habits that account for most avoidable losses. Long enough to be worth the read.

items.title: Introducing Concentrated Incentives on Saros DLMM
items.tldr: Streaming rewards only to liquidity sitting at the market price, rather than spraying them across the whole curve.

items.title: Building Internet Capital Markets: RWAs, Stablecoins and BTC
items.tldr: A founder's thesis piece on how those three pieces fit together on Solana. Opinionated rather than instructional, and clearer for it.

items.title: Ever Wondered What APY Really Means?
items.tldr: Vaults advertise 10%, 20%, sometimes 100%+ and the number rarely means what a reader assumes. Unpacks compounding, emissions and annualisation.

items.title: x402: The Payment Layer for the Agentic Internet
items.tldr: As tasks shift from humans clicking to agents executing, something has to settle payment machine-to-machine.

items.title: Navigating Risk in DeFi: How OneRouter Builds Resilience
items.tldr: Routing across protocols means inheriting the weakest one's risk. Covers how a router limits that exposure rather than assuming every venue behaves.

items.title: A Complete Guide to Solidity Security Audits for Web3 Protocols
items.tldr: What an audit involves from the protocol's side: how scope gets set, what reviewers will not look at, and how to read the report you get back.

items.title: Agentic AI Security Risks in Web3: What Protocols Need to Know
items.tldr: Agents acting onchain widen the attack surface in ways a point-in-time audit was never designed to catch.

items.title: Best Web3 Bug Bounties in 2026: The Highest-Paying Programs
items.tldr: Surveys what the top programmes pay across every major platform. More interesting as a read on how protocols privately price their own risk.

items.title: sBridge: Purpose-Built Interoperability for SVM Networks
items.tldr: A bridge designed for one virtual machine family rather than for everything. Narrowing the problem changes what security assumptions are available.

items.title: Seeding Real-Time Ideas on InfiniSVM
items.tldr: What applications become possible once execution is fast enough to feel synchronous, written as a survey of ideas rather than a product pitch.

items.title: What Is Selective Disclosure, and How Do Verifiable Credentials Reveal Only What's Needed?
items.tldr: Showing a driving licence to prove your age hands over your address too. Selective disclosure turns that into proving one fact and nothing more.

items.title: What Is Device Binding, and How Does It Stop a Stolen Digital ID Being Reused?
items.tldr: A digital credential that can be copied is worth very little. Device binding is the cryptographic layer tying one to a single phone.

items.title: Using a Mobile Driver's License at the Airport: How TSA mDL Acceptance Works
items.tldr: Behind one tap at a checkpoint sits a chain of trust and a pile of standards. Traces that chain, the clearest worked example of digital ID in use.

items.title: vsdCRV Incident Disclosure
items.tldr: A compromised deployer key used to forge unbacked tokens on Arbitrum, written up with the timeline and the fix.

items.title: Votemarket Incident Disclosure
items.tldr: Protocols that disclose properly, twice, are worth reading precisely because most disclose once and quietly.

items.title: Diversified Staking With MetaVaults
items.tldr: Routing deposits across several underlying vaults instead of running validators directly. What that spreads out and what it does not, for slashing.

items.title: Setting Up Per-Client MetaVaults
items.tldr: How one validator fleet can serve several clients with separate staking experiences. Operationally specific in a way most staking content avoids.

items.title: Leveraged osETH/WETH Looping Strategy on Gearbox
items.tldr: Walks a leveraged staking loop end to end with the actual numbers. Useful because it shows where the yield comes from and what liquidates it.

items.title: Cross-Chain Swaps Are Not a Feature, They're the New Default
items.tldr: Bridges, atomic swaps and resolver-based HTLC each handle custody differently, and the difference decides who holds your asset mid-transfer.

items.title: Do Cross-Chain Bridge Users Get Better DeFi Rewards?
items.tldr: Wallet data suggesting bridge users run more deliberate strategies, set against the fees that quietly erode the difference. Data-led rather than asserted.

items.title: DeFi Protocols Across Chains: Same Brand, Different Game?
items.tldr: A protocol on Ethereum and the same protocol on Base share a name and little else. Compares liquidity, fees and token availability across deployments.

items.title: Building the Hydra Transaction Stream Plugin
items.tldr: Extending Cardano's layer 2 with a plugin for streaming transactions. A concrete look at what Hydra makes possible and what it demands in return.

items.title: Building a Strategies Platform for Cardano DeFi
items.tldr: What has to exist before automated strategies can run on a UTXO chain, where the execution model differs sharply from account-based DeFi.

items.title: Deep Dive: Solana Onchain Activity
items.tldr: A monthly data read on what Solana is actually being used for, broken out rather than reported as one headline number.

items.title: Deep Dive: Solana Developers
items.tldr: Tracks developer activity rather than price or TVL, which tends to lead the other two. Worth reading for how the measurement itself is constructed.

items.title: Deep Dive: Solana DApp Revenue
items.tldr: Revenue is the least flattering metric to publish and the most informative. Breaks down which applications on Solana genuinely earn and how much.

items.title: Introducing TWAP Orders on Synthetix Perps
items.tldr: Time-weighted average price orders exist because pushing size through in one go moves the market against you.

items.title: Introducing Scaled Orders on Synthetix Perps
items.tldr: Rather than one large limit at a single level, a scaled order lays a ladder across a range. How execution shape changes your average fill.

items.title: Introducing ETH as Margin on Synthetix
items.tldr: The first non-stable asset accepted as collateral, which sounds simple and is not: posting a volatile asset as margin changes how liquidation has to work.

items.title: How to Avoid DeFi Liquidity Squeezes
items.tldr: Variable-rate pools like Compound and Aave can leave lenders unable to withdraw exactly when they most want to.

items.title: 3 Ways to Use Fixed-Rate Loans as a Passive User
items.tldr: Written for someone who wants a known rate and no daily management. Three concrete positions, with what each assumes about where rates go next.

items.title: 3 Ways to Use Fixed-Rate Loans as an Advanced User
items.tldr: The follow-up for people who will actively manage the position: leveraging the rate view itself rather than just locking one in.

items.title: What "Verifiable" Actually Means for Blockchain Data
items.tldr: Breaks down 1-of-N trust models, consensus and cryptographic verification as separate things, because they get used interchangeably and guarantee less.

items.title: Subgraphs or Substreams: Which Blockchain Data Solution Should You Choose?
items.tldr: Subgraphs give structured queryable data for user-facing apps; substreams push high-throughput pipelines.

items.title: GraphTally: How The Graph Solved Micropayments for the Machine Economy
items.tldr: Pay-per-request billing is being treated as new, but The Graph has settled micropayments this way in production since early 2025.

items.title: Inside Toros Bitcoin Short Volatility
items.tldr: Takes a structured product apart into its two components, a covered call position and an actively rebalanced short.

items.title: Hyperliquid-Powered Stock and Commodity Leveraged Tokens
items.tldr: 2x and 3x tokens on NVDA and the Nasdaq 100, built on perp markets. A concrete look at how leveraged exposure to equities gets wrapped into a single token.

items.title: Leveraged Gold Exposure on Ethereum and Arbitrum
items.tldr: Explains the wider project of turning complex leveraged strategies into one holdable token, and what gets abstracted away when you do that.

items.title: How to Verify Smart Contracts on OP Stack, Step by Step
items.tldr: Verification is what lets anyone read the source behind a deployed address. A walkthrough for OP Stack chains, where the process differs from mainnet.

items.title: Tracking Every OP Stack L1 to L2 Interaction
items.tldr: Deposits and withdrawals between layers are where rollup users most often lose track of funds. On monitoring that boundary continuously.

items.title: Batched L2 Details: The Explorer Feature You're Probably Missing
items.tldr: Rollups post transactions to L1 in batches, and most explorers hide that entirely. What batching does to cost and finality, and why seeing it matters.

items.title: Build Your First SubQuery Project in 10 Minutes
items.tldr: A short hands-on route into blockchain indexing: stand up a project and query it end to end, which teaches the data model faster than reading.

items.title: Why Newly-Launched Rollups and Appchains Need a Different Indexer
items.tldr: A new rollup has no indexing infrastructure on day one and no history to backfill. What an appchain needs from an indexer, and how that differs.

items.title: Beyond JSON-RPC: How Unified Data Schemas Simplify Multi-Chain Frontends
items.tldr: Building across many chains feels like translating a dozen languages at once. The case for normalising at the schema level, not in every component.

items.title: Live Smart Routing to the Best Web3 RPC Provider
items.tldr: Providers degrade at different times and in different regions, so the best endpoint is not a fixed choice.

items.title: Web3 Infrastructure Health Scorecard: A Deep Dive
items.tldr: Breaks down each pillar and metric used to judge whether infrastructure is healthy. Worth reading for the definitions, since uptime claims skip them.

items.title: Best Practices to Secure Your Assets
items.tldr: Written around setting up a clean machine, which is the right frame: most compromises trace back to the environment rather than the wallet itself.

items.title: Common Trends With Phishing in Web3
items.tldr: Short catalogue of the patterns that recur across Web3 phishing. Dated now, but the underlying tricks have proved remarkably durable.

items.title: Gas Sponsorship in Web3: Concepts, Tools, and Implementation
items.tldr: Covers relayers, meta-transactions, smart accounts and ERC-4337 as one connected story rather than four buzzwords, which is how they actually fit.

items.title: How Cross-Chain MEV and Private Order Flow Disrupt Chain Abstraction
items.tldr: Explains why abstracting chains away from the user makes the value being extracted underneath harder to see.

items.title: The Hidden Complexity of Solver Rebalancing in Intent-Based Systems
items.tldr: Solvers hold inventory across chains to fill intents, and that inventory drifts. Why rebalancing quietly decides whether an intent system stays fair.

items.title: An Explosion of Casual Games, Powered by AI
items.tldr: On what happens to game economies when production costs collapse and the supply of games rises sharply. Relevant well beyond the guild model.

items.title: 2025 in Review: The Rise of Casual Degen Gaming
items.tldr: A year of Web3 gaming summarised by someone with money on the outcome. A record of what the category did rather than what it promised.
